name: T-Bar Reverse Row
why: Back day version: a heavy row aimed at the lats.
setup: Chest on the pad, feet planted.
Start with arms fully straight.
form: Pull your shoulder blades back first, then drive the elbows toward your hips.
Squeeze 1 second at the top.
Lower under control until the arms are straight and the shoulder blades spread.
tips: Elbows close to the body = more lats. Elbows flared = more upper back (that's the version for traps days).
avoid: Lifting the chest off the pad to heave the weight.
Shrugging up instead of pulling back.
rangeOfMotion: Full stretch at the bottom to elbows just past the torso.

name: Single-arm Cable Lat Pulldown
why: Lats in the stretched position. Training one arm lets you reach further overhead.
setup: Pulley high, kneel or sit facing it.
One handle, arm fully up.
form: Let the arm reach up until the lat stretches.
Pull the elbow down to the side of the hip.
Return slowly to the full stretch.
tips: Think about pulling with the elbow, not the hand.
Pause 1 second in the stretch.
avoid: Twisting the torso to finish the rep.
rangeOfMotion: Arm fully overhead to elbow beside the ribs.

name: Single-arm DB Row
why: Lower lats. The elbow travels toward the hip in an arc.
setup: One hand and knee on a bench, or a hand on a rack, back flat.
DB hangs straight under the shoulder.
form: Pull the elbow back and up toward the hip.
Lower until the shoulder blade spreads forward.
tips: Pull to the hip, not the chest. Pulling to the chest shifts the work to the upper back.
avoid: Rotating the torso open to move more weight.
rangeOfMotion: Full hang to the DB at hip height.

name: Straight-arm Cable Pulldown
why: The only lat move with no biceps involvement. Takes the lats from stretched to fully contracted.
setup: High pulley, bar or rope.
Step back and hinge forward about 30°.
form: Keep the arms almost straight with a slight bend locked in.
Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze.
Let the arms rise back overhead to the stretch.
tips: A rope lets the hands finish slightly behind the hips for a harder squeeze.
avoid: Bending the elbows, which turns it into a triceps pushdown.
rangeOfMotion: Arms overhead to hands at the thighs.

name: DB Incline Curl
why: Arms hang behind the body, which stretches the long head of the biceps.
setup: Bench at 45–60°, lie back.
Arms hanging straight down, palms forward.
form: Curl without letting the elbows drift forward.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
tips: Keep the head and shoulders on the bench so the stretch stays.
avoid: Elbows swinging forward, which removes the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Full extension to full curl.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
why: Hardest near the bottom, so it trains the biceps lengthened.
setup: Armpits snug at the top of the pad, upper arms flat on it.
EZ bar is fine if a straight bar bothers your wrists.
form: Curl up, stop just before the forearms are vertical.
Lower slowly until the arms are nearly straight.
tips: Slow down most near the bottom. That's the part that builds it.
avoid: Dropping fast into the bottom (stresses the elbow).
Lifting the elbows off the pad.
rangeOfMotion: Almost straight arm to just short of vertical forearms.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
why: Your only direct front-delt work, plus triceps.
setup: Seat height so the handles start at chin level.
Back flat on the pad.
form: Press up to just short of a hard lockout.
Lower under control to chin level.
tips: Keep the ribs down. Don't arch off the pad to finish reps.
avoid: Half reps at the top only.
rangeOfMotion: Chin level to arms almost straight.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
why: Side delts with tension through the whole range, including the bottom.
setup: Low pulley, single arm, cable running behind your body.
Slight lean away.
form: Raise out to the side, leading with the elbow, to shoulder height.
Lower slowly, 2–3 seconds.
tips: Think of pushing the hand out wide, not up.
rangeOfMotion: Hand by the hip to shoulder height.

name: Lateral/Shrug Hybrid
why: Your locked-in heavy trap move: a partial lateral raise combined with a shrug.
setup: Heavy DBs at your sides.
Straps are fine if grip fails first.
form: Raise the arms out to about 30–45° while shrugging the shoulders to the ears.
Hold 1 second at the top, lower slowly.
tips: The goal is shoulders to ears. The arm height is secondary.
avoid: Turning it into a light lateral raise.
rangeOfMotion: Arms by the sides to about 45° with full shrug.

name: Barbell Shrug
why: Heavy upper-trap loading.
setup: Bar in front, overhand grip, just outside the thighs.
Stand tall.
form: Shrug straight up, pause 1–2 seconds.
Lower to a full stretch.
tips: Use straps so grip doesn't end the set before the traps do.
rangeOfMotion: Shoulders fully down to fully up.

name: Overhead Trap
why: Your lower-trap exercise. Raising the arm overhead makes the shoulder blade rotate up, and the lower traps work hardest above the head.
setup: Cable on the lowest setting.
Stand 3–4 feet away.
form: Sweep the arm up in a half circle until it's over your head.
Finish in a Y, slightly in front of your head, thumb up.
Pause 1 second at the top, lower slowly.
tips: At the top, reach up so the shoulder blade rotates fully.
Go light enough to reach the top every rep.
avoid: Arching the lower back to get the arm up.
rangeOfMotion: Hand low by the body to fully overhead.

name: Machine Reverse Fly
why: Rear delts in a fixed path.
setup: Chest on the pad, handles at shoulder height.
Slight bend in the elbows.
form: Sweep the arms back wide until they line up with the body.
Return slowly.
tips: Keep the shoulder blades from squeezing hard together. That keeps the work in the rear delts instead of the traps.
rangeOfMotion: Arms in front to in line with the torso.

name: Smith Squat
why: Heavy quad work. Stopping at parallel grows the quads about as well as going deep, with much less glute work.
setup: Feet shoulder width, roughly under or slightly in front of the bar.
Bar across the upper back.
form: Sit down until the thighs are parallel, no deeper.
Drive up through the mid-foot, knees following the toes.
tips: Feet more under the bar = more knee bend = more quads.
rangeOfMotion: Standing to thighs parallel.

name: Leg Extension
why: Isolates the quads with no glute involvement, which fits the plan.
setup: Back of the knee at the seat edge, knee lined up with the machine's pivot.
Ankle pad just above the ankle.
form: Extend until the knees are straight and squeeze for 1 second.
Lower slowly, about 2–3 seconds.
tips: Leaning back a little stretches the rectus femoris (the quad muscle that also crosses the hip) more.
avoid: Kicking the weight up and letting it drop.
Lifting the hips off the seat.
rangeOfMotion: From about 90° (or deeper if the machine allows) to fully straight.

name: Prone Leg Curl
why: Hamstrings in the short (contracted) position.
setup: Lie face down, knees just off the pad edge.
Pad above the heels.
form: Curl the heels toward the glutes.
Lower slowly to almost straight.
tips: Press the hips into the pad the whole time.
avoid: Dropping the weight on the way down.
rangeOfMotion: Almost straight legs to full curl.

name: Hip Adduction
why: Inner thighs. Large muscles that add thigh size without involving the glutes.
setup: Sit tall, pads on the inside of the knees.
Set the start as wide as you can control.
form: Squeeze the legs together and pause 1 second.
Open slowly back to the stretch.
tips: The stretched (wide) part does the most work. Don't cut it short.
avoid: Letting the weight stack slam at the open position.
Rocking the torso to move the weight.
rangeOfMotion: Widest controlled stretch to legs together.

name: Standing Calf Raise
why: Straight knees work the upper calf.
setup: Balls of the feet on the edge, knees straight.
form: Lower until the calves are fully stretched and pause 1–2 seconds.
Rise as high as possible.
tips: The paused stretch at the bottom matters most.
rangeOfMotion: Full stretch to full rise.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
why: Heavy vertical pull.
setup: Grip about 1.5× shoulder width.
Thighs locked under the pad, slight lean back.
form: Pull the bar to the upper chest, elbows down and slightly back.
Return until the arms are straight.
tips: Let the shoulders rise at the top for the full stretch.
avoid: Leaning way back and rowing it.
rangeOfMotion: Full stretch at the top to bar at the upper chest.

name: Cable Seated Row
why: Heavy horizontal pull.
setup: Neutral handle, feet on the plate, knees slightly bent.
form: Row to the lower ribs and squeeze 1 second.
Let the arms go straight and the shoulder blades spread.
tips: A small forward lean in the stretch is fine. Swinging back is not.
avoid: Using the lower back to throw the weight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight to handle at the belly.

name: EZ Bar Incline Tricep Extension
why: Long head of the triceps stretched with the arms angled back.
setup: Incline bench at 30–45°, lie on your back.
Arms angled slightly back past vertical.
form: Bend only at the elbows and lower the bar behind your head.
Extend back up.
tips: Keep the upper arms still. Only the forearms move.
rangeOfMotion: Deep stretch behind the head to straight arms.

name: Machine Dip
why: Heavy triceps compound.
setup: Sit upright.
form: Push down to a full lockout.
Return as deep as your shoulders allow.
tips: Staying upright keeps it triceps-focused.
rangeOfMotion: Deepest comfortable point to straight arms.

name: V-Bar Pushdown
why: Triceps with the arms at your sides.
setup: High pulley, V-bar.
Elbows pinned at your sides, slight forward lean.
form: Push down to full lockout and squeeze.
Let the forearms rise just above 90°.
tips: The lockout squeeze is the point of this one.
avoid: Leaning over the bar to push with body weight.
rangeOfMotion: Forearms just above parallel to arms straight.

name: Rope Face Pull
why: Rear delts and mid traps, plus shoulder health.
setup: Rope at face height.
form: Pull toward the forehead and split the rope apart.
Finish with hands beside the ears, elbows high.
tips: Light and controlled. The finish position matters more than the weight.
avoid: Leaning back to move heavy weight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight to hands beside the ears.

name: Lean-away Lateral Raise
why: Leaning away makes the bottom of the raise hard, so side delts work stretched.
setup: Hold a post with one hand, lean away 15–30°.
DB or cable in the free hand.
form: Raise to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
tips: Start the rep from a dead stop at the bottom.
avoid: Letting the lean change during the set.
rangeOfMotion: Hand across the body to shoulder height.

name: All-the-way-up Lateral Raise
aliases: All the way up lateral raise
why: Side delts up to shoulder height, then upper traps above it.
setup: Light DBs.
form: Raise out to the sides, past shoulder height, until near overhead.
Lower slowly.
tips: Use less weight than a normal lateral raise.
avoid: Swinging to get past shoulder height.
rangeOfMotion: Sides to almost overhead.

name: Kelso Shrug
why: Mid traps, an angle the shrugs miss.
setup: Chest-supported row machine, chest on the pad.
Arms straight, holding the handles.
form: Squeeze the shoulder blades back together without bending the elbows.
Hold 1 second, release forward.
tips: It's a short movement. Make the squeeze count.
avoid: Bending the elbows, which turns it into a row.
rangeOfMotion: Shoulder blades fully forward to fully back.

name: Single-arm Cable Reverse Fly
why: Rear delts with a cable, a second angle to the machine.
setup: Cable at shoulder height.
Grab the handle with the opposite hand, across your body.
form: Sweep the arm out and back at shoulder height, slight elbow bend.
Return across the body.
tips: Keep the shoulder down and the torso square.
rangeOfMotion: Across the body to in line with the torso.

name: Rope Overhead Tricep Extension
why: Long head stretched overhead.
setup: Face away from a low or mid cable.
Rope behind the head, elbows forward by the ears.
form: Extend fully overhead.
Lower into a deep stretch.
tips: Keep the elbows pointing forward and still.
rangeOfMotion: Deep stretch behind the head to straight arms.

name: DB Hammer Curl
why: Heavy neutral-grip curl. Builds arm thickness under the biceps.
setup: Neutral grip (palms facing in), elbows at your sides.
form: Alternate arms, curl to the shoulder.
Lower all the way.
tips: This is a heavy one. Add weight when you hit 10 clean reps on every set.
rangeOfMotion: Straight arm to full curl.

name: Leg Press
why: Second heavy quad move.
setup: Feet low on the platform, shoulder width.
form: Lower to about a 90° knee angle.
Press up without locking the knees hard.
tips: Feet low = more knee bend = more quads, less glutes.
avoid: Going deep enough for the lower back to round.
rangeOfMotion: About 90° at the knee to almost straight.

name: Seated Leg Curl
why: Hamstrings stretched. Grew more than lying curls in research.
setup: Lap pad tight, knees lined up with the pivot.
form: Curl fully.
Return slowly to straight legs.
tips: Leaning the torso forward increases the hamstring stretch.
avoid: Letting the weight yank the legs straight.
rangeOfMotion: Straight legs to full curl.

name: Seated Calf Raise
why: Bent knees switch work to the soleus, the lower calf.
setup: Knees bent 90°, pad on the lower thighs.
form: Lower to a full stretch and pause.
Rise as high as possible.
tips: Pause at the bottom every rep.
rangeOfMotion: Full stretch to full rise.

name: Cable One-Arm Tricep Kickback
why: Triceps in the short (fully contracted) position, the one angle the other triceps moves miss.
setup: Low pulley, single handle, hinge forward.
Upper arm pinned beside the torso, parallel to the floor.
form: Extend the elbow until the arm is straight and squeeze 1 second.
Bend back to about 90°.
tips: Light weight. The squeeze at full lockout is the whole point.
rangeOfMotion: About 90° at the elbow to fully straight.
